question: What will the ratio be of the simple interest earned on a given amount at the same interest rate over 6 years compared to that earned over 9 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a fixed principal and interest rate, Simple Interest (SI) is directly proportional to the time period.

⇒ SI ∝ Time

⇒ SI₁ : SI₂ = Time₁ : Time₂

⇒ SI₁ : SI₂ = 6 : 9 = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time period 1 (T₁) = 6 years

Time period 2 (T₂) = 9 years

Principal (P) and Rate of Interest (R) are constant for both cases.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 6 Yrs
 
 SI = 6PR ÷ 100
 9 Yrs
 
 SI = 9PR ÷ 100
 
• 
 Ratio → 6 : 9 → 2 : 3

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI for 6 years (SI₁) = (P × R × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ SI for 9 years (SI₂) = (P × R × 9) ÷ 100

⇒ Ratio = SI₁ : SI₂

⇒ Ratio = [(P × R × 6) ÷ 100] : [(P × R × 9) ÷ 100]

⇒ Cancelling common terms (P, R, and 100) from both sides:

⇒ Ratio = 6 : 9

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 3

**∴ The correct answer is 2:3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Proportionality in Simple Interest

When Principal and Time are constant, Simple Interest is directly proportional to the Rate of Interest (SI ∝ R). When Rate and Time are constant, SI is directly proportional to the Principal (SI ∝ P).

Total Amount Formula

Total Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI) = P × [1 + (R × T) ÷ 100].

SI vs CI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for exactly 2 years is calculated directly by the formula: D = P × (R ÷ 100)².
